blocks.h2: How to Check for a Hidden Leak
blocks.body: Your water meter can tell you a lot. Turn off every faucet and appliance that uses water, then look at the meter. Most have a small dial or triangle that spins when water is moving. If it's spinning with everything off, water is leaking somewhere. Next, shut off the valves under toilets and check again. If it stops, a toilet is the culprit. If it keeps moving, call us and we'll track down the leak.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a Leak Repair
blocks.body: Finding the leak is often the biggest part. A visible leak is quick. A hidden one inside a wall or under a slab takes testing. The pipe material and how much needs replacing matter too. We locate it, explain the options and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Leak Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.q: How do you find a hidden leak?
items.answer: With acoustic tools, pressure tests and moisture readings, so we open as little as possible.

items.q: Do you repair the water line from the street?
items.answer: Yes, the part on your property. The village handles its side.

items.q: Why do I keep getting pinhole leaks?
items.answer: Usually aging copper. Repeat leaks suggest the pipe is near the end of its life.
Policies vary. Check with your agent.

items.q: Can a slab or underground leak be found without digging?
items.answer: Usually. Acoustic tools and pressure tests narrow it down before we open anything.

items.q: Can you check the water service line for leaks?
items.answer: Yes. Wet spots in the yard or a meter that keeps moving can point to it.
